Create read-only ellmer tools for multi-stream reviewed memory

Source: R/memory-tool.R
graft_tools.Rd

Create a pair of ellmer::ToolDef tools so an agent can list eligible reviewed streams for one host-chosen purpose and recall any eligible stream on demand. Unlike graft_tool(), the model chooses which stream to recall, but its argument is never authority by itself: every call checks the host's streams allowlist (when supplied) and evaluates eligible(stream) afresh before reading retained content.

Usage

graft_tools(
  store,
  purpose,
  eligible,
  streams = NULL,
  list_name = "list_project_memory",
  recall_name = "recall_project_memory",
  max_streams = 100L,
  max_text_bytes = 64 * 1024L
)

Arguments

store

A store returned by graft_store() or graft_store_postgres(). The handle remains private inside the tools.

purpose

The consultation purpose fixed by the host application.

eligible

A required host-supplied one-argument function taking a stream name and returning one TRUE or FALSE value. Evaluated for each candidate stream during listing and again on every recall invocation.

streams

Optional host allowlist of stream names: NULL to discover accepted streams in store for purpose, a character vector of allowed stream names, or a zero-argument function returning a character vector of currently allowed stream names.

list_name

Tool name for listing eligible streams. Defaults to "list_project_memory".

recall_name

Tool name for recalling one stream. Defaults to "recall_project_memory".

max_streams

Maximum eligible accepted streams returned by the listing tool. Defaults to 100L.

max_text_bytes

Maximum total UTF-8 bytes of text previews returned for one recall invocation. Defaults to 64 KiB.

Value

A named list of two ellmer::ToolDef objects (list_name and recall_name), ready for chat$set_tools(), deputy::Agent$new(), or mcptools::mcp_server().

Details

The listing tool returns only streams whose current decision is "accept" for purpose and for which eligible(stream) returns TRUE. Withdrawn streams, streams for other purposes, ineligible streams, and total store counts are never disclosed. When streams is supplied, only those stream names are inspected.

The recall tool accepts one stream string argument, verifies it against streams (when supplied) and eligible(stream), and returns the same bounded ellmer::ContentToolResult, JSON payload, @extra$graft metadata, and optional shinychat display metadata as graft_tool(). A stream not in the host allowlist fails with the same graft_ineligible_error as an ineligible stream.
